chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married five women in a single contract, he said: 'He may release whichever one he wishes and keep the four.' And the Magian, when he embraces Islam and has more than four wives, should keep four of those whose marriage is permissible and release the others.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who marries five women in one contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the mechanism of polygyny adjustment, emphasizing that the limit of four is enforced through immediate release (*takhliyah*) rather than requiring a new contract for each wife. It extends this fiqh principle to converts from Zoroastrianism, illustrating the juristic consensus that the four-wife limit applies universally upon conversion, regardless of prior marital status. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence to maintain existing marriages while adhering to the Quranic cap.
